solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bob finds two causes of power failure

parts.note: a cut in the supply is one thing that stops the power
a short circuit, a short for short, is another thing that trips the power

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a pair of reasons why the electricity went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name, but it is the verb for trimming hair or a story short.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob hair or a tale is to trim it, abbreviating it abruptly.

clue.text: Agreement to give son in marriage

indicators.note: the letter for son goes inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: A consent given for a son to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in agreement, all as one.

clue.text: Accident to make light of?

definitions.meaning: a fall or mishap, as from a horse or bike
a twist of paper or a wood sliver used to carry a flame and light a fire or pipe

explanation.definitionFit: A spill is both a tumble and a paper taper for lighting things.

clue.text: Too much rudder admits first watch to master

indicators.note: the joined words let a letter in between them, as a door admits a visitor

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdone
the helm is the steering gear of a ship

indicators.note: only the opening letter of watch is taken

explanation.surface: Excess steering lets in a sentry before the captain takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm someone is to overpower or master them completely.

clue.text: Servant troubles making these establishments harder to run nowadays

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of the word are disturbed

explanation.surface: Problems with staff make running these places harder today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making these' joins the wordplay to the definition, which describes pubs as struggling businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are pubs or inns, businesses widely said to be struggling to stay open today.

clue.text: Seizure, or an attempt at seizure

definitions.meaning: a sudden fit, as in a heart ...
an assault aimed at capturing a position

explanation.definitionFit: An attack is both a medical fit and an assault meant to capture something.

clue.text: Admit everything with cry of pain

parts.note: all means everything
ow is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: Confess everything with a yelp of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something in the sense of accepting it is to allow it.

clue.text: Come about a printer's setting

indicators.note: a printer setting type arranges letters, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word is used whole, its S included

explanation.surface: A typesetter at work arranging the type.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire is to happen or emerge, the sense of something occurring.

clue.text: Musical piece that may take longer if cut short

definitions.text: Musical piece that may take longer if cut short

parts.words: Musical piece that may take longer if cut short
parts.note: drop the last letter of this orchestral work and you have a whole evening's performance, which lasts longer

explanation.surface: A piece of music that paradoxically runs longer when shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut its final O and the work becomes CONCERT, a full programme that takes longer than one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical composition for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: Excellent to include it, within limits

indicators.note: the word for excellent takes the other word inside it

parts.note: fine means excellent, very good

explanation.surface: Praising something as excellent but keeping it within bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finite is bounded, having limits rather than going on for ever.

clue.text: English football team at home getting penalty finally for foul play

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, called Villa for short
in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: only the end letter of penalty is used

explanation.surface: An English club at its home ground concedes a penalty late for a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club from Birmingham; 'foul play' means wickedness here, not a foul in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Villainy is wicked or criminal behaviour, which foul play describes.

clue.text: One after another

parts.note: a phrase for things in sequence, read as someone who goes after another person

explanation.definitionFit: A follower is a person who goes after or pursues someone else, a disciple or chaser.

clue.text: Point to Elizabeth's favourite part of old England

parts.note: W, west, is a compass point
the Earl of Essex was a favourite courtier of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: Gesturing towards the Queen's preferred region of ancient England.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was Elizabeth I's favourite; 'Point' is not a gesture but a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the West Saxons in southern England.

clue.text: As in pre-stage make-up?

indicators.note: the words are made up afresh, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Something resembling what actors put on before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' both signals the rearrangement and, with the whole clue, describes theatrical cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasepaints are the cosmetics actors apply before a stage performance.

clue.text: Planned on a magnificent scale, but badly organised

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grand scheme that was poorly executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means impressive and ambitious in scale, often excessively so.

clue.text: Given freedom at bottom of page — nothing new to say

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for freedom sits below the letter for page

parts.note: latitude is freedom of action, scope given

explanation.surface: Someone granted licence at the foot of a page has run out of fresh things to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, a statement with no fresh insight.

clue.text: Like Biblical swine, eager and wild

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: The pigs of scripture rushing headlong, keen and frenzied.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels Jesus sent demons into the Gadarene swine, which rushed into the sea; the word now means headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadarene describes the herd of pigs at Gadara in the Gospel story.

clue.text: Sort of error that could make one late

definitions.text: Sort of error that could make one late

parts.words: Sort of error that could make one late
parts.note: late here means dead, as in the late Mr Smith, not behind time

explanation.surface: A kind of slip that might make someone arrive behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' tempts one to think of delay; it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal mistake is an error that causes death or ruin.

clue.text: Topic for study may need pencil and paper — no ruler

definitions.text: Topic for study may need pencil and paper
definitions.meaning: a school discipline such as maths, studied with pencil and paper
a person under a monarch rather than one who rules

explanation.definitionFit: A subject is both an area of study and a person ruled by a sovereign.

clue.text: Copper to rebuke one coming between vicar and his flock

definitions.text: one coming between vicar and his flock

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold

explanation.surface: A policeman told off by a man who interrupts a priest and his congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant clergyman, ranking below the vicar but above the parishioners.

clue.text: Club porter

parts.note: not a doorman at a gentlemen's club but someone who carries golf clubs

explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag and clubs round the course.

clue.text: Spot-on old-time variety performance?

parts.note: ex means former, from an earlier time
an act is a turn in a variety show

explanation.surface: Praising a perfect vaudeville turn from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely correct, which spot-on also means.

clue.text: Mentions how one rears children

definitions.meaning: to raise a topic in conversation
one raises children, the parent's job

explanation.definitionFit: Bringing something up means raising it in talk, and also raising a child.

clue.text: Key list put out for government securities

parts.note: G is a musical key

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An important register issued about state bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilts are British government bonds, gilt-edged securities.

clue.text: Give an order — to paint?

definitions.meaning: award someone an order or medal
to paint or paper a room

explanation.definitionFit: To decorate is both to honour with a medal and to paint a room.

clue.text: Take articles from magazine?

parts.note: not reading pieces in a periodical but removing cartridges from a gun's magazine

explanation.definitionFit: To unload a gun is to remove its ammunition, emptying the magazine.

clue.text: Desert fault

definitions.meaning: to abandon one's side or country

explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to desert a cause, and a defect is a flaw.

clue.text: Girl's second and he's getting sporting prize

parts.note: Thea is a girl's name
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A girl comes second and a boy wins the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ASHES is the cricket trophy contested by England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the prize in the England–Australia Test cricket series.
